lines: An AI agent wrote 404 lines for one date picker. Ponytail made it 23.
Ponytail is one prompt that makes your agent think like the laziest senior dev.
You know him. Long ponytail, oval glasses. Fifty lines in, one line out.
That idea has 156k stars on GitHub.
Before it codes, it climbs a ladder. Does this need to exist? Is it in the codebase? Only then: the minimum that works.
Ask for a date picker: your agent installs flatpickr, writes a wrapper, debates timezones. Ponytail writes one line.
A native date input. The browser already has one.
Real agent, real repo, twelve tickets. Ponytail cut code by 54%, cost by 20% and time by 27%.
Lazy, not negligent: security and accessibility are never cut. Still 100% safe.
Pair it with caveman: one shrinks the talk, one shrinks the code.
Two commands install it in Claude Code. Codex and others work too.
Code you never wrote scales infinitely. Send this to someone who writes fifty lines.
Ponytail. MIT licensed: the shortest license that works.
